v.rationale: All three versions have nearly the same design: a #[Scope] scope with a created_at index, lazyById, a Cache::lock shared with manual runs, onOneServer, dry-run before confirmation, and keeping the row when the file can't be deleted. All test suites pass (17, 17 and 18 tests). I ran four throwaway probes against each version, then deleted them. Three passed for all three versions: a real permission-denied directory on a local disk (row kept, the rest processed, exit 1), more than 1000 failing rows followed by one good row (no infinite loop with lazyById), and --days=0 and --days=1.5. The fourth probe, production with -n, could not run in PHPUnit because the mocked console output doesn't respect -n. I ran it on the real CLI instead, against a temporary SQLite database: all three refuse with exit code 1. The seeded export row wasn't created in that run (the setup step failed quietly), so the CLI checked only the exit codes, not whether rows were kept; the in-suite tests cover that. impl-2 ranks first: it uses ConfirmableTrait as intended, returns INVALID for bad --days, has broad tests (both confirmation answers, -n refusal, a mock of the Filesystem contract) and no bugs; its main flaw is the anonymous command subclass used to test confirmation. impl-3 has equally sound behaviour and cleaner tests, but it hand-rolls production confirmation instead of using ConfirmableTrait. impl-1 adds a Europe/Copenhagen timezone nobody asked for, so the job runs at 02:00 UTC instead of 03:00. It also uses a by-reference closure with a partially selected model, swaps the Storage facade for duck-typed anonymous classes in its tests, and has no test for the interactive 'yes' path.
